page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose, 64-core Arm-based cloud instance powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with dedicated physical cores and no simultaneous multithreading, it provides 64 discrete physical cores. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It bundles 3,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel throughput and high I/O capability, balanced by modest single-threaded performance. The server achieved top-quartile results in multi-core stress testing with a stress-ng score of 97,021.02, software compilation with Clang reaching 43,260.0, and small-block cached memory bandwidth of 3,782.85 GB/sec. Combined with 25 Gbps networking, it recorded 72.77 million Redis SET operations per second and 45.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, tasks constrained by single-thread throughput, such as single-core Geekbench (973.0) and single-threaded gzip compression, placed in the lower tiers.

The m6gd.16xlarge offers resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out workloads by leveraging high core counts and low-latency local NVMe storage. Direct-attached flash eliminates network transit latency for scratch storage, making the instance well suited for distributed in-memory or on-disk caches, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation jobs, high-traffic web servers, and distributed data processing. Workloads requiring high single-core frequencies or specialized x86 vector instruction sets are less suited to this architecture.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by 64-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, 256 GB of system RAM, 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves strong parallel execution in Clang compilation and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside top-tier static web throughput at 45.93 GB/sec and 72.77 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded performance remains modest, reflecting an architectural emphasis on multi-core efficiency over single-core clock frequency. The integrated local NVMe storage and balanced memory ratio deliver practical compute density for distributed caching, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-volume web serving, and database applications utilizing local scratch storage.
